newsitem.title: USA: US Apr spot natgas little changed from March index.
newsitem.headline: US Apr spot natgas little changed from March index.

text.p: U.S. spot gas prices for April 1 were talked steady to slightly higher from March indices, but most traders were tentative to close many fixed-priced deals prior to the futures expiry.
April Louisiana Gulf prices mirrored futures and March indices at $1.79-1.80 per mmBtu, while prices for Tuesday held in the mid-to-high $1.80s.

In south Texas, April prices were talked in the high-$1.60s, up about five cents from March indices. Swing prices were slightly weaker in the high-$1.70s to low-$1.80s as normal to below-normal temperatures covered the state.
As of 1337 EST, NYMEX's April Henry Hub natgas was down six cents at $1.78 per mmBtu.

At the New York city-gate, where temperatures are forecast to climb to above normal Wednesday through Friday, swing prices settled to about $2.15-2.17, down about five cents from Friday. Prices for April 1 delivery were even with March indices around $2.10.
In the Southwest, extended heat and low storage levels boosted April pricing over March bidweek levels.

April 1 prices at the southern California border were talked in the low-$1.70s, up about 10 cents from March indices. However, swing prices eased by a few cents to about $1.80 despite continuing warmer-than-normal weather.
Meanwhile, Permian basin prices for Tuesday were little changed in the high-$1.60s to about $1.70, while the April 1 market hovered in the low-$1.60s.
San Juan prices for April 1 gained about 10 cents on March indices to the mid-$1.50s.

In the Midcontinent, swing prices remained in the mid-$1.70s, while April pricing was talked in the high-$1.60s, up two to five cents from March 1 levels. Northern at Demarcation for next month was quoted at $1.69-1.70.

Temperatures throughout the Midwest are forecast to remain mostly above normal through the weekend, with some areas expected to experience temperatures as much as 25 degrees Fahrenheit above normal Friday.
